To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a solid‐phase desorbing dosing system was successfully applied in 2 flow through bioconcentration studies to generate stable concentrations in the test medium of 4 highly hydrophobic chemicals (HOC) (hexachlorobenzine, o‐terphenyle, polychlorinatedbiphenyl 153, anddibenz[a,h]antracene) without using solubizing agents.
the bioconcentration of 3 of 4 HOC test substances could be determined in fish exposed to test solutions prepared via the solid‐phase desorbable dosing system.

we developed a dosing system that is able to provide stable aqueously dispersed HOCs for bioconcentration studies and that the system was successfully applied to 4 HOC compounds with log KOW values between 5.5 and 7.8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a solid‐phase desorbing dosing system for the bioconcentration of highly hydrophobich organic chemicals (HHC) in fish.
the development of a new dosing system that enables the preparation of stable aqueous solutions of highly hydrophophic organic chemicals (HHCs).

the development of a novel dosing system that allows the generation of aqueous test media with stable analyte concentrations for the determination of bioconcentration factors in fish according to OECD guideline 305.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of solvents is a valid alternative to the use and application of a desorption system.
the solid‐phase desorbing dosing system is a suitable tool for bioconcentration testing of HOCs with log KOW values > 5.

the results of the present study indicate that the solid‐phase desorbent dosing system is a feasible alternative for the preparation of aqueous test solutions for the bioconcentration test in fish with HOCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solid‐phase desorber is a suitable alternative for preparing aqueous concentrations of hydrophobic organic compounds.
the system is suitable for the generation of stable aqueous concentrations and that the system represents a viable alternative for the use of solublizing agents in the preparation of test media.
the use of the solid phase desorption dosing systems for HOCs in the range of log KOW 4 to 8 can be recommended for the bioconcentration studies in fish.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of solid‐phase desorbers for the preparation of aqueous test media is a viable alternative to solubilizing agent use.
we developed a new dosing method for the bioconcentration of highly hydrophobichydrophobic chemicals in fish.
we have developed a new system to generate stable aqueous concentrations without using solubilizating agents.
